aphrodisias.name: Aphrodisias
aphrodisias.slogan: A marble city that carved its own gods.
aphrodisias.line: Its stadium, about 270 metres long, held roughly 30,000 spectators, and the whole site became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2017.

didymaapollo.name: Temple of Apollo at Didyma
didymaapollo.slogan: Nineteen-metre columns still guarding an oracle.
didymaapollo.line: Work on the temple went on for more than 600 years and it was never finished; each Ionic column stands about 19.7 metres tall.

guvercinada.name: Pigeon Island Castle
guvercinada.slogan: A little fortress at the end of a causeway.
guvercinada.line: The castle and garrison on Pigeon Island were rebuilt and expanded in 1834, and the island is joined to Kuşadası by a causeway.

aydinmuseum.name: Aydın Archaeological Museum
aydinmuseum.slogan: Home ground of the world's oldest complete song.
aydinmuseum.line: The Seikilos epitaph, the oldest surviving complete musical composition, was found at Tralles, today's Aydın, around 1883.

miletustheatre.name: Theatre of Miletus
miletustheatre.slogan: A giant marble bowl that once looked out over a busy harbour.
miletustheatre.line: Miletus was the home of Thales, often called the first philosopher; silt has since pushed the sea about 8 km away.

waive_area_cap: Aphrodisias, Didyma and Miletus are the valley's three great ancient sites
